positioning: The clown who never grew up and never wants to.
story: A Boxer does not walk into a room. It arrives. The whole back end wiggles, the front paws pat the air, and the face says the party can finally start.

The breed took shape in Germany in the late 1800s. Breeders in Munich crossed the old Bullenbeisser, a big-game hunting dog, with the English Bulldog. They wanted strength, courage, and a short muzzle that could hold on.
They got all of that. They also got a clown. Boxers stay playful for years. People call them the Peter Pan of dogs, and the name fits.
Boxers carried messages and stood guard in the world wars. American soldiers brought them home, and the breed took off. The AKC recognized it in 1904.
At home, a Boxer is half guard and half goof. It watches the door like a sentry, then licks the visitor. It leans, it snorts, and it dances the kidney bean, curving its whole body in joy.
Give a Boxer exercise, shade, and a seat near you. It will repay you in wiggles. It never forgets Father’s Day.
rank_cap: The Peter Pan of dogs, forever playful (AKC)
fblocks: No one is sure. The likeliest story is the way a Boxer bats with its front paws, as if sparring.
Dampf von Dom, the first AKC champion Boxer, in 1915. Boxers also carried messages for the German army in World War I.
Flat faces overheat fast, so shade and water matter. Boxers can inherit heart disease, so ask about screening.
A sleek, short coat in fawn or brindle, often with white markings. Mostly white Boxers are not allowed in the show ring.
Fifty to eighty pounds. Created in Germany in the late 1800s. Recognized by the AKC in 1904.
days: Father’s Day. The old Boxer has the porch glider, and nobody will argue.
The Boxer began in Munich, from the old Bullenbeisser and the English Bulldog.
Boxers carried messages in World War I. Brave dogs, and still silly at home.
A Boxer’s jaw looks fierce. Its soul is a marshmallow. Guard the hot dogs anyway.
Stop at the zinnias. Watch the bee. Nothing needs you for a full minute.
Short noses mean Boxers overheat fast. Keep the hose handy.
Puppies pile into Dad’s empty chair. He will sit somewhere else tonight.
last_walk:
The porch lights come on, and the fireflies rise.
Rocky and Roxie walk the cul-de-sac side by side. She skips. He plods. Both tails keep time like metronomes. A Boxer ends the day the way it began, wiggling. Someone left a light on. Home is two doors away.
